UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                       BEFORE THE
                         FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

                                                         )
Midcontinent Independent System                          )                      Docket No. ER26-3813-000
   Operator, Inc.                                        )
                                                         )

               NOTICE OF INTERVENTION AND COMMENTS IN SUPPORT OF
                      THE ORGANIZATION OF MISO STATES, INC.

           The Organization of MISO States, Inc. (“OMS”) submits this Notice of Intervention and

Comments regarding proposed tariff revisions filed by the Midcontinent Independent System

Operator, Inc. (“MISO”) with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“Commission”) in the

above-captioned proceeding.1 On September 21, 2026, MISO filed proposed revisions to

Attachment X – Generator Interconnection Procedures (“GIP”) of its Open Access Transmission,

Energy, and Operating Reserves Markets Tariff (“Tariff”) with two main objectives: 1.) to reform

the Generator Interconnection Queue (“GIQ”) restudy process for all Definitive Planning Phase

(“DPP”) cycles; and 2.) to reduce the size of its 2022-DPP Cycle (“GIQ Reform Filing”). With

respect to the second objective, MISO proposes to allow all Interconnection Customers in the DPP-

2022 Cycle a one-time, unconditional opportunity to withdraw from the queue penalty-free at

Decision Point II. In exchange, the threshold for penalty-free withdrawal after Decision Point II

would be increased.2 These provisions, if approved, would encourage the timely exit for unviable

projects and, thereby, accelerate the study process for later DPP cycles.

           OMS recognizes that a functional interconnection queue is essential to reliability, resource

adequacy, competition, and effective planning. Since the DPP-2022 Cycle predates MISO’s recent


1
    Midcontinent Indep. System Operator, Inc., Legacy Queue Acceleration and Restudy Limitation Proposal, Docket

2

 queue reforms and continues to experience delays and uncertainty, OMS supports targeted

measures to address the legacy backlog. Specifically, OMS tentatively supports a one-time,

penalty-free withdrawal opportunity for DPP-2022 projects, an increase in the penalty-free

withdrawal threshold from 35% to 50%, and a defined post-Phase 3 withdrawal window for future

DPP cycles followed by a final restudy when necessary to address identified reliability impacts.

OMS views these measures as practical complements to MISO’s broader queue reforms that can

reduce unnecessary study work, provide greater certainty to interconnection customers, and help

ensure that newer reforms can operate effectively.

    I.     NOTICE OF INTERVENTION

           OMS is a non-profit, self-governing organization comprising representatives from the

seventeen regulatory bodies with jurisdiction over entities participating in MISO and serves as the

regional state committee for the MISO region. OMS coordinates regulatory oversight among its

members, makes recommendations to MISO, the MISO Board of Directors, the Commission, and

other relevant government entities and intervenes in proceedings before the Commission to express

the positions of OMS members. As such, OMS files its Notice of Intervention in this proceeding

under Rule 214(a)(2) of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure.3

           Service of pleadings, documents, and communications in this proceeding should be made

on the following:

      II.   COMMENTS

           OMS has consistently supported efforts to establish a more efficient, predictable, and

manageable GIQ process. In its prior comments supporting MISO’s GIQ Cap proposal, OMS

recognized that the size of the interconnection queue had reached an unmanageable level and

supported measures to bring the queue to a size at which MISO could conduct realistic studies and

process interconnection requests more effectively.4 OMS similarly supported MISO’s GIQ

“quality” reforms, including measures intended to ensure that projects entering the queue are

sufficiently mature and viable to proceed through the interconnection process.5 In these and other

filings, OMS recognized that a functional interconnection queue is essential to resource adequacy,

reliability, competition, and the ability of states and Load Serving Entities to plan for and procure

needed generation.

           While those reforms are important for establishing a more sustainable process going

forward, they did not apply retroactively to the DPP-2022 Cycle – the subject of this filing. The

current condition of MISO’s DPP-2022 demonstrates that additional action is necessary. Years of

cascading delays in older DPP cycles have contributed to MISO’s inability to timely process

subsequent queue cycles and have created substantial uncertainty for interconnection customers,

Transmission Owners, Load Serving Entities, and state regulators.6 MISO’s creation of the

Expedited Resource Addition Study process and its recent announcement that the application

deadline for DPP-2026 has been moved to January 15, 2027, further demonstrate the continuing

effects of the legacy backlog.

    Notice of Intervention and Comments of OMS, Docket No. ER24-341-000 (filed Dec. 4, 2023).

                                                            3
        OMS therefore tentatively supports MISO’s proposal to both allow a one-time, penalty-

free withdrawal in DPP-2022 and limit post-Phase 3 restudies to circumstances in which a

reliability impact is identified through an appropriate reliability screen. OMS believes this

approach can materially accelerate the processing of legacy queue cycles while preserving MISO’s

responsibility to identify and address reliability concerns. OMS urges the Commission to approve

MISO’s proposal and supports MISO’s continued efforts to develop complementary measures that

can accelerate the resolution of the legacy backlog while protecting projects that remain in the

queue from inappropriate or avoidable cost impacts.

       A.      DPP 2022 One-Time Withdrawal Opportunity

       OMS tentatively supports MISO’s proposal to provide, for the DPP-2022 Cycle, a one-

time, penalty-free withdrawal opportunity for all Interconnection Customers at Decision Point II.

OMS also supports increasing the threshold for penalty-free withdrawal and milestone-payment

refunds from 35% to 50% of combined Network Upgrade and Affected System costs, measured

from Phase II through the beginning of GIA negotiations.

       The DPP-2022 Cycle presents an appropriate opportunity for targeted relief. A one-time

opportunity to withdraw without penalty would allow projects that are no longer viable to exit the

queue without perpetuating the cycle of late-stage withdrawals and restudies that has contributed

to the legacy backlog. This targeted relief is consistent with OMS’s longstanding position that the

size and composition of the interconnection queue must be managed so that MISO can devote its

resources to projects that are potentially viable to proceed. Should this withdrawal opportunity

prove effective with DPP-2022, OMS would support applying this same principle to additional

cycles in follow-up filings. MISO’s more recent reforms will remain ineffectual until these legacy

queue cycles are cleared.



                                                4
        B.      A Defined Withdrawal Process for Future DPP Cycles

       For future DPP cycles, OMS is not opposed to MISO’s proposal to establish a single

withdrawal window after Phase 3, followed by a final restudy upon its conclusion, if necessary.

OMS agrees that post-Phase 3 restudies should be focused on circumstances in which additional

study is necessary to address identified reliability impacts. Limiting restudies in this manner would

allow MISO and the Transmission Owners to reduce unnecessary study work while preserving its

ability to identify and address legitimate reliability concerns.

       A defined final withdrawal opportunity would also provide greater certainty to both MISO

and Interconnection Customers. Once the withdrawal window closes and any necessary final

restudy is completed, the remaining projects can proceed without the continuing cycle of

withdrawals and restudies that has contributed to delays in the legacy queue.

       OMS is concerned, however, that the proposed withdrawal framework could have

downstream cost-allocation consequences that are not yet sufficiently understood. MISO should

explain how its screening and subsequent reliability studies will identify upgrades that remain

necessary following withdrawals, and how those costs will be reassigned through later DPP cycles,

affected system studies, and MTEP. Greater transparency through this process – along with the

large load study process and assumptions – is necessary to ensure costs appropriately follow the

projects that cause them and do not ultimately shift to transmission customers and retail rate payers.

       C.      The Legacy Queue Must Be Resolved for Recent Reforms to Succeed

       OMS’s prior support for the Queue Cap and Queue Quality reforms reflects a consistent

principle: MISO needs a manageable and sufficiently mature interconnection queue to produce

timely and meaningful study results. The current legacy queue presents a different but related

challenge. Projects that entered the queue under prior rules continue to generate cascading delays



                                                  5
 that consume resources and impede the processing of subsequent cycles. Until that backlog is

substantially reduced, the benefits of MISO’s recent queue reforms are expected to remain

constrained.

       MISO’s proposal provides a targeted means of addressing this problem. The DPP-2022

penalty free withdrawal would provide an immediate opportunity to reduce the number of projects

remaining in a legacy cycle, while the proposed single withdrawal window and final restudy

process would help prevent the same cycle of repeated withdrawals and restudies from continuing

in future DPP cycles. As such, OMS supports these measures as a practical complement to the

Commission’s and MISO’s broader interconnection reforms.

 III. CONCLUSION

       OMS tentatively supports MISO’s proposed measures to reduce the legacy interconnection

queue and establish a more predictable process for future DPP cycles. For the DPP-2022 Cycle,

OMS supports the proposed one-time, penalty-free withdrawal opportunity and the increase in the

applicable cost threshold from 35% to 50%. For future DPP cycles, OMS is not opposed to a single

post-Phase 3 withdrawal window followed by a final restudy focused on identified reliability

impacts, provided MISO’s study process ensures that necessary upgrades are identified and

resulting costs remain with the appropriate cost-causer rather than shifting downstream to

transmission customers. OMS’s support for these measures builds on its prior support for MISO’s

Queue Cap and Queue Quality reforms. Those reforms established important mechanisms for

managing the queue going forward, but targeted action is needed now to address the legacy backlog

that predates them.

       Finally, OMS recognizes the timing constraints associated with this filing but remains

concerned that increasingly compressed stakeholder processes limit states and other stakeholders’



                                               6
 ability to meaningfully evaluate significant Tariff changes. OMS encourages MISO and the

Commission to ensure sufficient time for meaningful stakeholder review wherever practical to

ensure downstream ramifications do not hinder progress and speed to power.

       OMS submits these Comments because a majority of OMS members support this filing.

This should not be construed to mean that all OMS members agree with all comments herein.

Individual OMS members reserve the right to file separate comments. In recognition of such, the

following members voted in support of this filing:
